correctness.rationale: For compact supp(mu) subset {(x,y,z):0<x,y,z<1} and theta on R/pi Z, log x,log y,log z are bounded C1 on a neighbourhood of the support; invariance gives three exact zero drifts. Their pairwise differences yield c(X-Z)=e(Y-X) and A=(c+e)(Y-X)+e(X-Z). Because Q=c²+ce+e²>0, the claimed gaps follow; summing the three gives (3+c-e)(X+Y+Z)=3+A. The phase rotation theta_dot=2omega has unique Haar invariant probability for omega>0; x<1 and gamma>0 imply A>0. For strictly positive full-period periodic orbits the log drifts integrate to zero. Independent SymPy reconstruction from the exact ODE produced five identically zero residuals, nonzero matrix determinant -(3+c-e)Q, face signs and three rational sample checks. Experiments are supporting checks; the proof is analytical.

value.rationale: The population means are natural observables in a three-species recurrent competition model. Their exact gap ratio is the biologically and dynamically motivated heteroclinic attraction parameter delta=c/e from the primary paper, independent of period, forcing amplitude, frequency or choice of compact-interior stationary law; gamma>0 enforces a definite mean ranking. This exact finite-amplitude model-specific diagnostic is potentially reusable in interpreting invariant measures and recurrent trajectories even though the derivation uses familiar log balances and offers no new attractor existence theorem. It is not merely a normalization or verification result.

final_claim: In the Rodrigues periodically forced May–Leonard flow with 0<e<c<1, gamma>0 and omega>0, every invariant probability measure compactly supported inside 0<x,y,z<1 obeys Y-X=cA/Q, X-Z=eA/Q, X+Y+Z=(3+A)/(3+c-e), A=gamma int (1/x-1) sin² theta dmu>0 and Q=c²+ce+e², hence Y>X>Z and (Y-X)/(X-Z)=c/e. Same for strictly positive phase-locked periodic orbits with period averages. No result is asserted for boundary-accumulating measures or existence of qualifying recurrent states.
limitations: The theorem is conditional on existence of a compact-interior invariant probability measure or suitable periodic orbit.
